title: Configurable input bindings + mouse sensitivity + sprint key
description:
Right now everything is hardcoded — WASD/Space/F live as Keys.* lookups inside PlayerController, FlyCamMouseTrap, and DungeonKeyGuy. Mouse-look sensitivity is hardcoded at 0.1f deep inside Camera3D.mouseMove. We need a small binding/configuration layer so different scenes (and eventually the user) can map actions without editing engine internals. 

Proposed structure: an InputBinding map keyed by a stable Action enum (MOVE_FORWARD, MOVE_BACK, STRAFE_LEFT, STRAFE_RIGHT, JUMP, SPRINT, TOGGLE_FLY, ...) returning a list of GLFW key codes. PlayerController, KeyGuy subclasses, and Camera3D's mouseMove sensitivity all consume from this map. Default map matches today's hardcoded behavior so nothing regresses. 

On top of that, add: 
- SPRINT action (Shift) doubles walk speed when held 
- Configurable mouse-look sensitivity (currently fixed at 0.1°/pixel in Camera3D.mouseMove) — float on the input config, default unchanged 
- Future: gamepad input via GLFW joystick API, but start with keyboard/mouse
definition-of-done: 1. Action enum in ixdar.platform.input covering current actions (movement, jump, fly-toggle, sprint). 2. InputBindings record/class mapping Action -> int[] keyCodes, with a static DEFAULTS instance matching today's behavior. 3. PlayerController takes an InputBindings reference and reads pressedKeys via bindings.isPressed(action, set). 4. DungeonKeyGuy's F-toggle reads from bindings (TOGGLE_FLY action). 5. SPRINT action implemented in PlayerController — multiplies horizontal velocity by ~2 while held. 6. Mouse-look sensitivity exposed on Camera3D (replace the hardcoded 0.1f) with a setter. 7. Existing tests pass without modification using the DEFAULTS bindings.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: PlayerController with default bindings behaves identically to current pre-config tests. 2. Unit test: PlayerController with a custom binding (e.g. swap W and S) moves opposite to default. 3. Unit test: SPRINT held doubles horizontal motion per frame. 4. Manual test: launch Ixdar Dungeon Player, hold Shift while walking — speed visibly increases. 5. Manual test: change Camera3D mouse sensitivity via setter, confirm rotation rate scales accordingly.
todos: Define Action enum + InputBindings type in ixdar.platform.input
Refactor PlayerController to read pressedKeys via InputBindings
Refactor DungeonKeyGuy to read TOGGLE_FLY via InputBindings
Add SPRINT action wired to LEFT_SHIFT, multiplies walk speed in PlayerController
Replace Camera3D.mouseMove's hardcoded 0.1f with a configurable mouseSensitivity field + setter
Migrate existing tests to use DEFAULTS bindings; add binding-override tests
